Implementation record (2026-08-21). The plan passed review at rv10 after one blocking finding was closed and three advisory ones were designed out; this comment keeps the trail.

- The rv9 BLOCK (criterion G6) was a broken acceptance oracle, not a broken plan. AC-1 asserted `key == hash(wire_body)`, but the key is `landed_text` — the marker-STRIPPED decode of `to_wire(wire_body)` — while `wire_body` is the marker-BEARING pre-encode text, so the two can never be equal. AC-1 now states the equality that actually holds and that the Jira-side inbound key is symmetric with: `key == landed_text == strip_marker(decode(what the transport received))`.

- The "one codec, one set of bytes / the send path MUST NOT re-encode" constraint was internally inconsistent and has been replaced. Cloud's wire is JSON-serialised ADF, so `codec.to_wire` MUST run at send time; there is no verbatim-bytes path to have. What must not happen is a fit that MOVES the bytes after the key was taken. The adapters therefore keep their defensive fit (it still covers direct callers) and the leaf pins the property that makes the key sound: re-fitting an already-fitted body is byte-identical, asserted on each deployment's real fitter rather than assumed.

- The third `add_comment` call site — `dispatch_one.py:636`, the illegal-transition status fallback — is deliberately out of scope and is now named as such. It posts a short literal that never passes through the differ and has no `wire_body`; it keeps reaching the adapter's own fit.

- The truncation-suffix literal (three definitions) and the `32767` occurrences were both dropped from scope, and the reasons recorded. `test_rich_text_codec.py:69-71` documents that `adf._ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX` and `rich_text._WIKI_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX` are defined independently ON PURPOSE — "the shared layer must not import the Cloud module" — and pins them to one value; collapsing that is a package-layering decision, not part of this leaf. The `32767` occurrences are sourced product knowledge (the DC `jira.text.field.character.limit` default, cited to JRASERVER-28519), so the earlier grep-count oracle could never have passed. Dropping both also removed the E4/E6 advisories, which were about an oracle (`git diff --stat`) that could not distinguish prose from code.

Implementation: `fit_for_send(body, *, sanitizer, codec, inbound_mapper) -> FittedComment(landed_text, wire_body)` in `outbound_comments.py`; `_diff_comments` keys on `landed_text` (byte-identical to the previous `compare_body`, so the diff decision is unchanged) and puts `wire_body` on the mutation; `dispatch_one.py` and `dispatch_apply_phases.py` read `entry.get("wire_body") or entry.get("body", "")`.

Mutation evidence for the new suite (each mutation applied to the live code path, then reverted; the whole file is green before and after):
- drop `"wire_body"` from the mutation entry -> 12 failures incl. `test_over_limit_comment_converges_after_one_pass` on all four [deployment x path] cases.
- create path stops falling back to `body` -> exactly the two `test_an_entry_without_wire_body_still_sends_its_body[*-create]` cases fail.
- `dispatch_apply_phases` ignores `wire_body` -> exactly the six update-path cases fail; create stays green.
- `fit_for_send` stops decorating -> `test_key_equals_the_marker_stripped_decode_of_what_the_transport_received` and the corpus test fail on the marker assertion.
- `fit_for_send` skips the fit -> the "over-limit body must reach the wire fitted" and idempotence assertions fail, and the corpus test fails on "the wire text must already be fitted".
- the differ keys on the raw body instead of `landed_text` -> the corpus test fails on "a landed corpus body must not be re-emitted".

The first corpus test drafted here was a tautology (it recomputed both sides through `fit_for_send`) and survived every mutation; it was rewritten to three per-body statements — marker survives, wire is already fitted, a landed body is not re-emitted — and now dies under three separate mutations.
